The BRQS module for the MY component

Source: R/adult-MY-BRQS.R
BRQS.Rd

Implements the MY component using a BRQS (Blood-feeding / Resting / gravid Queue / Sugar-feeding) model of adult mosquito ecology and infection dynamics. Mosquitoes cycle through sugar-feeding (S), blood-feeding (B), resting (R), and gravid (Q) states. Each behavioral state is tracked as uninfected (u), exposed (y), or infectious (z).

State Variables

Su, Bu, Ru, Qu

uninfected mosquitoes in the sugar-feeding, blood-feeding, resting, and gravid states

Sy, By, Ry, Qy

exposed mosquitoes in each behavioral state

Sz, Bz, Rz, Qz

infectious mosquitoes in each behavioral state

S, B, R, Q

total mosquitoes in each behavioral state, derived by get_MY_vars.BRQS

M

total adult mosquito density, derived during parsing

Y

total exposed and infectious mosquito density, derived during parsing

Z

total infectious mosquito density, derived during parsing

Dynamical Terms

Lambda or \(\Lambda\)

adult mosquito emergence rate, supplied by ramp.xds::Emergence

kappa or \(\kappa\)

net infectiousness, supplied by ramp.xds::Transmission

Parameters

f

blood feeding rate — use ramp.xds::setup_f or ramp.xds::setup_blood_feeding_rates

q

human fraction — use ramp.xds::setup_q or ramp.xds::setup_human_fractions

g_b, g_q, g_s, g_r

mortality rates in the blood-feeding, gravid, sugar-feeding, and resting states

rho

rate of leaving the sugar-feeding state to blood-feed

zeta

rate at which blood-feeding mosquitoes take a sugar meal

xi

rate of leaving the resting state

eta

rate of transition from resting to gravid

nu, theta

parameters governing the egg-laying / gravid state

delta

fraction of gravid mosquitoes returning to blood feeding

omega

fraction of emerging mosquitoes entering the sugar-feeding state

tau

rate of progression from exposed to infectious

eip

extrinsic incubation period; \(\tau\) is its reciprocal

sigma_b, sigma_q, sigma_s

emigration rates in the blood-feeding, gravid, and sugar-feeding states

mu_b, mu_q, mu_s

fraction of emigrants lost in each dispersal state

K_b, K_q, K_s

dispersal matrices for the blood-feeding, gravid, and sugar-feeding states

eggsPerBatch

number of eggs per batch

After basic setup, change_MY_pars.BRQS can be used to change parameter values. The model routes emergence between the blood-feeding and sugar-feeding states using \(\omega\); behavioral transition rates \(\rho\), \(\zeta\), \(\xi\), \(\eta\), \(\nu\), and \(\theta\) govern movement among the four behavioral states.

Survival and Dispersal

Blood-feeding, gravid, and sugar-feeding mosquitoes have separate demographic matrices, \(\Omega_b\), \(\Omega_q\), and \(\Omega_s\). Each combines its state-specific mortality, emigration rate, emigration-loss fraction, and dispersal matrix.

Blood Feeding

Blood feeding occurs from the blood-feeding state at rate \(f\). A human blood meal transmits infection to a susceptible mosquito with probability \(\kappa\); the force of infection is \(fq\kappa\).

Dynamics

The derivative method tracks the twelve state variables listed above. Mosquitoes move among the four behavioral states, acquire infection during human blood feeding, and progress from exposed to infectious at rate \(\tau\). The implementation is dMYdt.BRQS.

Infective Biting

The patch-level human biting density, fqM, is based on blood-feeding mosquitoes; infective biting density, fqZ, is based on infectious blood-feeding mosquitoes. F_fqM.BRQS and F_fqZ.BRQS compute these quantities. ramp.xds::compute_EIR combines fqZ with the biting distribution matrix and resident-bite fraction to compute stratum-level EIR; ramp.xds::F_hbr uses fqM to compute stratum-level HBR.

Egg Laying

Gravid mosquitoes lay eggs at rate \(\nu\); egg production is the number of gravid mosquitoes multiplied by the oviposition rate and eggs per batch: $$G=\nu(Q_u+Q_y+Q_z)\Gamma.$$ F_eggs.BRQS computes \(G\), which is passed to ramp.xds::EggLaying for distribution among aquatic habitats.
